title: Data Retention Policy
content: All client data must be retained for a minimum of 7 years in compliance with Luxembourg financial regulations (CSSF Circular 12/552). Data classified as personal under GDPR must not be retained beyond the defined purpose period. Archival systems must be encrypted at rest using AES-256. Data owners are responsible for scheduling automated deletion workflows upon expiry. Exceptions require written approval from the Chief Data Officer. Annual reviews must confirm that retention schedules remain aligned with applicable regulatory requirements. Backup copies are subject to the same retention rules as primary data. The Central Data Office maintains a retention register updated quarterly.

title: Data Classification Framework
content: Nexum Financial S.A. classifies all data into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Public data may be shared externally without restrictions. Internal data is for employee use only. Confidential data requires encryption in transit and at rest using approved algorithms (AES-256 or RSA-2048 minimum). Restricted data requires multi-factor authentication, audit logging, and explicit approval from the Data Governance team for each access event. All new datasets must be classified within 30 days of creation. Partner-only data may only be accessed by Partners and above with dual authorisation. Data stewards are responsible for verifying classification accuracy during quarterly reviews. Misclassification must be reported within 48 hours of discovery.

title: Personal Data Processing Policy
content: Processing of personal data must comply with GDPR Article 6 lawful bases. A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is mandatory for high-risk processing activities as defined in GDPR Article 35. Data subjects have the right to access, rectify, erase, and port their personal data. Requests must be acknowledged within 5 working days and fulfilled within 30 calendar days. Cross-border transfers outside the EEA require Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or equivalent safeguards approved by the Data Privacy Officer. PII must be pseudonymised or anonymised wherever technically feasible without impacting business requirements. Consent records must be stored for the duration of the processing plus 7 years. The Data Protection Officer must be consulted for all new data processing activities involving sensitive categories. Automated decision-making affecting individuals requires explicit consent and an explanation of the logic involved.

title: Access Control and Privileged Access Policy
content: All system access follows the principle of least privilege as defined in ISO 27001. Privileged access to production data requires dual approval from line manager and Data Governance team. Access reviews are conducted quarterly; unused accounts are disabled after 45 days of inactivity. Service accounts must not have interactive login capabilities. All privileged sessions are recorded and stored for 12 months. Violations trigger immediate access revocation and a mandatory incident report to the CISO within 2 hours. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is enforced across all production systems; roles are documented in the RACI matrix maintained by the CDO. Password complexity requirements: minimum 12 characters, at least one uppercase, one digit, and one special character. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all privileged accounts and for remote access to any system classified CONFIDENTIAL or higher.

title: Data Quality Standards Policy
content: All critical data assets must meet six quality dimensions: Completeness (>98%), Accuracy (>99%), Consistency, Timeliness, Uniqueness, and Validity. Data stewards are responsible for monthly quality reports submitted to the CDO office. Failing datasets trigger a remediation workflow with a 14-day SLA. The Data Quality Score (DQS) is published on the Data Catalog dashboard every Monday morning. Root cause analysis is mandatory for DQS scores dropping below 90% on Tier-1 assets. Data quality metrics must be automated and integrated into CI/CD pipelines for all new data pipelines. Third-party data must pass quality validation before ingestion. Exceptions to quality thresholds require written approval from the relevant Domain Data Steward and must be logged in the risk register.

title: AI Model Governance Policy
content: All AI and ML models used in client-facing or regulated processes must undergo a Model Risk Assessment before deployment. Models must be documented with model cards including training data provenance, intended use, known limitations, and bias metrics aligned with EU AI Act requirements. Quarterly performance reviews are mandatory. High-impact models covering credit, risk, or compliance decisions require sign-off from the Partner-level Model Risk Committee before go-live. Models consuming personal data must be registered with the DPO and undergo a DPIA. Explainability requirements apply to all automated decisions affecting clients. Adversarial testing and red-teaming exercises are required for models classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act. Retired models must be archived with full documentation for 5 years.

title: Data Lineage and Provenance Policy
content: All Tier-1 critical data assets must have documented end-to-end data lineage covering: source system, ingestion method, transformation logic, quality checks applied, and consuming systems. Lineage documentation must be updated within 5 business days of any pipeline change. Automated lineage harvesting is preferred over manual documentation. Lineage metadata must be stored in the enterprise data catalog and version-controlled. Orphaned datasets (no documented lineage) must be flagged for review within 30 days of discovery. Lineage audits are conducted semi-annually and results shared with the CDO and relevant domain data stewards. For regulatory reporting data, lineage must be traceable to the ultimate source record with no gaps.

title: DORA Operational Resilience and ICT Risk Policy
content: In compliance with the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), all critical ICT systems supporting financial services must have documented business continuity plans and disaster recovery procedures. ICT third-party providers must be assessed annually against concentration risk criteria. Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) for Tier-1 systems: 4 hours; Recovery Point Objectives (RPO): 1 hour. Cyber incident reporting to CSSF must occur within 24 hours for major incidents. ICT risk is managed within the Enterprise Risk Framework and reviewed quarterly by the CRO. Penetration testing of critical systems is mandatory bi-annually. Supply chain risk assessments cover all vendors with access to RESTRICTED or higher data.
